front_blocks.md: 25.0 cm<sup>3</sup> of 0.050 mol dm<sup>-3</sup> Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> is neutralised by 20.0 cm<sup>3</sup> HCl. What is the concentration of HCl? (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H<sub>2</sub>O + CO<sub>2</sub>)

back_blocks.md: Moles Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> = 0.025 x 0.050 = 0.00125 mol. Moles HCl = 2 x 0.00125 = 0.00250 mol. Concentration HCl = 0.00250/0.020 = **0.125 mol dm**<sup>**-3**</sup>.

front_blocks.md: In a reaction of 9.2 g Na with 8.0 g S to form Na<sub>2</sub>S, which is the limiting reagent? (2Na + S → Na<sub>2</sub>S; A<sub>r</sub>: Na = 23.0, S = 32.1)

back_blocks.md: Moles Na = 9.2/23.0 = 0.40 mol. Moles S = 8.0/32.1 = 0.25 mol. To react 0.40 mol Na requires only 0.20 mol S. S is in excess, so **Na is the limiting reagent**.
